findings.title: raw_html cook method stores and renders unsanitized remote HTML
findings.body: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so posts created by `TopicEmbed.import` keep whatever HTML came from the remote source as their `cooked` value. The RSS path (`Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` -> `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`) passes the feed body through with no tag/attribute whitelist at all (only `import_remote` filters tags via ruby-readability), and the resulting `cooked` is emitted with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb as well as in normal topic rendering. A hostile or compromised feed (or an XSS-laden page scraped from the embeddable host) can therefore inject `<script>`/`onerror` payloads that execute for every visitor of the forum. The imported HTML should be run through the existing sanitizer (e.g. Sanitize with a whitelist) before being stored as cooked.

findings.title: Stray `if` in `<%- end if %>` breaks template compilation/output order
findings.body: Line 6 is `<%- end if %>`, which compiles to the Ruby fragment `end if` with no condition. Ruby then continues the modifier-`if` onto the next generated statement, so the logo `link_to` on line 8 becomes the *condition* of the conditional block: the logo is appended to the buffer before the button, and the whole if/else is executed only if that append returns truthy. Depending on the ERB engine this is either a SyntaxError (500 on every embed request) or silently wrong markup ordering. The `if` is a typo and should be removed, leaving `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: `post.present?` does not detect a failed PostCreator run
findings.body: `PostCreator#create` returns the (unsaved) Post object even when creation fails — it raises `ActiveRecord::Rollback` internally, which is swallowed, and the returned post has errors and a nil `id`/`topic_id`. `post.present?` is therefore true for failed creations, and the following `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: nil, post_id: nil, ...)` blows up with a NOT NULL/validation error, masking the real failure (e.g. a title that is too long or a rate limit). Check `post.persisted?` (or `post.errors.blank?`) instead, and bail out gracefully otherwise.

findings.title: `open(url)` used without requiring 'open-uri'
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` but topic_embed.rb only requires 'nokogiri'. `open-uri` is only required in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, which is not loaded on the `retrieve_topic` -> `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` path (that path only requires 'topic_retriever'/'topic_embed') unless feed polling happens to be enabled. Without open-uri loaded, `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a file name and raises `Errno::ENOENT`, so on-demand embed retrieval (and the disqus thor task) fails. Add `require 'open-uri'` to this file.

findings.title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
findings.body: The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. After the substitution `src.sub(/^\/+/, '')` the result becomes `http://host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, i.e. a broken link/image for any feed that uses protocol-relative references (common for CDN-hosted assets). Protocol-relative URLs should be left alone or prefixed with the scheme only.

findings.title: Existing embed with a deleted post raises NoMethodError
findings.body: In the update branch `post = embed.post` can be nil (post hard-deleted, or a previous import that stored a bogus post_id). `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then fails with a NoMethodError inside a Sidekiq job, and the embed row is never repaired. Guard for a missing post and either recreate the topic or skip.

findings.title: `i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds, aborting the whole poll
findings.body: SimpleRSS exposes RSS 2.0 item bodies as `description` (and `content_encoded` for content:encoded); `item.content` is only populated for Atom feeds. For a plain RSS 2.0 feed `i.content` is nil and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError. Because the job is declared `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the exception kills the entire poll and no items are ever imported; the same exception on a single malformed item also aborts the remaining items in the loop. Fall back to `i.description`/`i.content_encoded` and skip (rather than abort on) items with no body.

findings.title: Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE can permanently block retrieval of a URL
findings.body: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` is not atomic. If the process dies, the Redis connection fails, or the job is killed between the two calls, the key stays forever with no TTL, so `retrieved_recently?` returns true for that embed_url for the rest of the Redis instance's life and that page's discussion can never be retrieved (the embed iframe is stuck on the loading page). Use `$redis.set(key, "1", nx: true, ex: 60)` (or SETEX) instead.

findings.title: Full feed poll executed inline during embed retrieval
findings.body: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs the complete RSS/Atom poll synchronously (HTTP fetch of the feed plus creation/revision of a topic for every item) inside the `retrieve_topic` job each time an unknown embed_url is requested and feed polling is enabled. One cold embed view can therefore trigger a multi-second-to-minute import, and many concurrent unknown URLs will import the feed repeatedly in parallel (no locking), duplicating work and hammering the feed source. Enqueue the poll instead, or guard it with the same throttle used for HTTP retrieval.

findings.title: `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid header value
findings.body: `ALLOWALL` is not a defined X-Frame-Options directive. Per the HTML spec/most current browsers an unrecognized value is treated as `DENY` (some older browsers ignored it), so setting this can actively prevent the page from being framed — exactly the opposite of the intent — and makes embedding fail on the browsers that follow the spec. To allow framing, delete the header that the default Rails/Discourse middleware set (`response.headers.delete('X-Frame-Options')`) and, if restriction is wanted, use a CSP `frame-ancestors` directive with the embeddable host.

findings.title: Loading page is cached for 1 minute but reloads itself after 30 seconds
findings.body: `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied to both branches, including the `render 'loading'` branch. The loading template reloads the iframe after 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), so the reload is served from the browser cache and shows the same "Loading Discussion..." page even after the topic has been retrieved; the user waits at least two cycles. Either skip caching (or use a much shorter max-age) when rendering the loading page, or make the reload cache-busting.

findings.title: Spec stubs TopicView.new to return nil, so the rendered template raises
findings.body: `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` has no `returns`, so `@topic_view` is nil. The default `best` template then evaluates `@topic_view.posts.present?`, raising NoMethodError on nil during render, which makes the example (and the assertions in the `after` block) fail rather than verify the success path. The mock needs to return a double exposing `posts`/`topic`, or the spec should use `render_views false` with an explicit template stub.

findings.title: `force: true` added to an already-released migration can drop a populated table
findings.body: Editing the existing CreateTopTopics migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` means that any environment which re-runs this migration (schema reload, `db:migrate:redo`, re-running from a reset schema_migrations) will silently `DROP TABLE top_topics` and all its rows instead of failing loudly. The same pattern is used in the new 20131217174004_create_topic_embeds migration. `force: true` has no benefit in a forward migration and should be removed.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any origin that is a substring of the configured `discourseUrl` rather than comparing origins for equality (and would also accept a message whose origin happens to be a prefix such as `http://discourse.example.co`). It also throws if `discourseUrl` is undefined. Compare `e.origin` against the origin parsed out of `discourseUrl` exactly.

findings.title: request.referer interpolated into a JS string with HTML escaping
findings.body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` applies HTML escaping inside a `<script>` block, where entities are not decoded. A referer containing `'` produces the literal `'` in the JS string (wrong targetOrigin), and a referer ending in a backslash escapes the closing quote, producing a JavaScript syntax error that kills the resize script. Use `escape_javascript` (`j`) and, better, pass only the scheme+host of the referer since postMessage expects an origin, not a full URL.

findings.title: Disqus import loses created_at and the --category option
findings.body: The thread import was switched to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which drops the previous `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, so imported topics are now dated at import time instead of the original Disqus thread date, and the removed `--category` option means imported topics can no longer be placed in a category. If these behaviours are intentionally dropped, the option removal should at least be reflected in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (accepting `created_at`/`category`) so existing import workflows are not silently degraded.
